replies.text: RC must be much bigger than 1 microsecond and much smaller than 200 microseconds. Too small and the carrier ripple comes through; too big and the capacitor can't discharge fast enough to follow the envelope down, so you get diagonal clipping.
replies.label: window-both
replies.note: Both limits and both reasons: the ok answer.

replies.text: Between 1 µs and 200 µs, because the diode needs about 1 µs to switch on and the capacitor is damaged if it charges for longer than 200 µs.
replies.label: window-no-why
replies.note: Router discipline: right numbers, wrong physics. Label the reasoning (partial), not the numbers (ok).

replies.text: As the modulation index approaches 1, the largest RC that avoids diagonal clipping shrinks towards zero, but RC still has to be much larger than the carrier period to hold the peaks. So no time constant satisfies both, and the envelope gets distorted.
replies.label: tradeoff
replies.note: Mechanism and consequence: the ok answer.
